newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK APT seeks waiver on 3-yr trading record - paper.
newsitem.headline: HK APT seeks waiver on 3-yr trading record - paper.

text.p: Satellite owner and operator APT Satellite Co Ltd will apply for a waiver of a Hong Kong listing rule that companies seeking listing have a trading record of at least three years, the Oriental Daily said Friday.
An initial hearing over the application would be held next week by the listing committee of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the paper quoted a source as saying.
"Once it passes the hearing, underwriting will proceed in full speed," the source was quoted on Friday as saying.
Beijing-controlled APT needs such a waiver because, although it has been established for more than four years, its first satellite, Apstar 1, was launched only in 1994.
Hong Kong Stock Exchange officials declined to comment and said they could not disclose the agenda of the committee.

Market rumours said APT Satellite has named Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette the sponsor of its initial public offering in Hong Kong and the United States. The company is expected to raise US$200 to US$300 million to repay loans and buy satellites.

APT is owned by China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, Chinese General Company of Aeronautics Industry and investors from China, Singapore, Thailand, Macau and Taiwan. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
